Today (November 5, New Calendar) the Church remembers the Holy Martyrs Galaction and his wife Episteme.

Galaction was born in Emesa to pagan parents who could not have children. A monk named Onuphrius told his mother that if they accepted Christ she would bear a child. She was baptized and bore a son, and his father too came to faith.

Galaction married a pagan maiden, Episteme, out of obedience to his father, and in time brought her to Christ and baptized her himself. The two resolved to remain in virginity and settled in separate monastic communities near one another.

When Galaction was seized in a persecution, Episteme asked her abbess’s blessing to join him. She boldly confessed Christ, and after many tortures husband and wife were beheaded together.
